legalName: Erasure After a Nolle, and Motion to Nolle a Continued Charge, C.G.S. § 54-142a(c)
publicName: Records erased after a case was nolled
mechanism: Where a charge has been nolled, records shall be erased once thirteen months have elapsed since the nolle. Separately, where a charge was continued at the prosecutor's request and thirteen months have passed with no prosecution or other disposition, the charge shall be nolled on motion of the arrested person, and erasure then follows the nolle rules. The second is an affirmative motion the participant can make; it is the one part of this track that is not passive.

rationale: The registry declares outputStrategyDeclared 'composed' with compositionMode 'alternative' and two branches, of which only the automatic-erasure branch is available:true.
The automatic branch requires no filing at all, so its required output is a participant instruction, not a document.

The § 54-142a(c)(2) motion branch is recorded as potentially custom_pleading and expressly not inherently guidance-only, but held: no form was located and the current caption, venue, service and clerk practice must be approved first. It is therefore a pleading_document unit with a blocked implementation, and nothing is drafted.

A third filing possibility — the pre-1 April 1972 petition — appears in the registry only as a packet instruction with no vehicle stated. It is carried as a third unit with a blocked implementation so that it is not silently omitted.

authoritySpine.description: Erasure thirteen months after a nolle. Police and court records and records of any state's attorney pertaining to a nolled charge.
Where a charge was continued at the prosecutor's request and thirteen months have passed with no prosecution or other disposition, the charge shall be nolled on motion of the arrested person.
No court fee is charged in any court with respect to any petition under § 54-142a.
Official source recorded on the track, retrieved 2026-07-30.
